title: Pegboard fit test: the shared hook peg + pin
subtitle: Built only from tools/pegboard.py, the pegs every catalog part uses · hung on your board (Menards 3/16" white, 1" grid) · X out from the board, Z up · mm

Hook leg rise above hole centre

scale_note: Real size. Pin 6.1 mm, hook 5.7 mm sloped 12° (your steel hook's wire is 5.53; prints at 5.53 and 5.9 were loose). The board uses your measured 1/4" holes on 1" centres; its thickness is the listing's 0.155".
notes: v4: the hook is now 5.7 mm and slopes up 12° through the board (like your steel hook's S-bend); the pin stays 6.1 mm. A rock-in simulation, calibrated on your v4/v5 hook prints, showed the old level 6.1 mm hook jams after ~3° of tilt. Check: it rocks on easily and the pin is snug. Then try the gauge for the pin size. Earlier: v3: pegs go from 5.9 to 6.1 mm, and there's a new peg gauge (green): a strip with straight pins at 6.0, 6.1, 6.2, 6.3 and 6.4 mm, each labelled. Its pins are spaced off the 1" grid so you try each in a hole on its own. Print it with the same filament and settings as your parts, then tell me the snuggest pin that still goes in by hand. That becomes the peg size for every catalog part.
